verdicts.reason: A has a sensible left-to-right flow (can → headline/copy → CTA), but the Shop Sale pill is jammed against the right edge and overlaps the decorative circle, and WEEKEND ONLY plus the legal line are shrunk to near-illegible fine print. B starts the reading order with the CTA, which is jammed against the left edge, and its copy almost touches the button. It also leaves a dead gap between the text and the can, and the legal text is just as tiny.

Both use the same broken layout: the CTA pill is pinned to the left edge with no margin and the headline and copy are butted against it. A wide empty band separates the text from a small can, and the legal line is unreadably small. The only differences are tiny shifts in the can's position, so neither is meaningfully better.

A is badly broken: the body copy runs straight into a two-line WEEKEND ONLY, the headline crowds the CTA, and the legal text is crammed into the circle at the far right. B has a clean can → text → CTA flow, with flaws: the CTA is tight to the right edge over the circle, and the urgency line and legal text are tiny.

A shrinks the 20% off headline until it barely outranks the body copy, so WEEKEND ONLY competes for attention. Its text is jammed against the edge-hugging CTA, and the can floats in empty space. B keeps a stronger headline but has the same flaws: the CTA is crammed against the left edge, the copy touches the button, there's a dead gap before the can, and the legal text can't be read.
